sources.story_title: News trigger — Alaska Municipal League conference, Fairbanks. GVEA COO Nathan Minnema on large loads: “That would determine if we have the ability to serve it or not.” MOA Policy Director Nolan Klouda on the Anchorage framework.

Layers 1-4 (PRIMARY) — AO 2026-27 text amending AMC Title 21. Data center defined at 20 MW peak demand; data centers made a conditional use in I-1/I-2/I-3; mandatory written system-capacity statement from the electrical utility; wastewater utility burden shift. NOTE: recovered document is the as-introduced version (reading 2026-02-17); enacted 2026-03-27, 10-2.

sources.outlet: Municipality of Anchorage, Office of Community Planning and Development
sources.story_title: Layers 5 and 7 (PRIMARY) — conditional use permit process. “No matter how many Commissioners are present it takes 5 yes votes to approve.” Appeal to the Board of Adjustment via the Municipal Clerk.
Layer 3 actor identity (PRIMARY) — “Chugach is the largest member-owned electric cooperative in Alaska”; territory extends from Anchorage to the northern Kenai Peninsula.
Layer 6 (PRIMARY) — Alaska water rights. “Public notice is required if the appropriation is greater than 5,000 gpd.” (AS 46.15 / 11 AAC 93)
Post-enactment corroboration (SECONDARY) — independently confirms the 20 MW threshold, the 200-foot setback and the capacity-demonstration requirement in the enacted ordinance.
